boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Southwestern rituals, from a century-old tower-signing rite to student research and finals-week karaoke.

cards.title: Homecoming at its 1909 birthplace
cards.subtitle: Annual campus-and-alumni gathering
cards.notes: Plan around the fall weekend: Southwestern documents its 1909 Homecoming origin and recent programming for students, alumni, families, and friends.
cards.short_summary: A long-running reunion weekend rooted in Southwestern’s documented 1909 Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern states that it celebrated Homecoming in 2024, 115 years after SU invented the tradition in 1909.
cards.access_notes: Programming and registration vary by year; check the University’s current Homecoming information.

cards.title: Pass the light at Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Lois Perkins Chapel each December
cards.notes: Attend the December lessons-and-carols service, then join the candle lighting and outdoor closing circle if you are comfortable with a faith-based event.
cards.short_summary: A 1915-era chapel service that ends with shared candlelight and carols.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern describes Candlelight as a beloved tradition begun in 1915, with candles lit one by one and a closing outdoor circle of carols.
cards.access_notes: Held every December in Lois Perkins Chapel; the service is Christian in content.

cards.title: Watch the SING! skit showdown
cards.subtitle: Greek-life musical comedy competition
cards.notes: Catch the annual themed show in Alma Thomas Theater to see student organizations combine live singing, costumes, choreography, and campus-specific comedy.
cards.short_summary: A student-organization performance competition documented at Southwestern since 1979.
cards.evidence_claim: The Megaphone reports that SING! has entertained Southwestern since 1979 through Greek-life sketch-comedy competition.
cards.source_title: SING 2026: Dungeons, Dinosaurs, and a Dorm’s Worth of Mold
cards.access_notes: Ticketing and participation details vary by year; performances are intended for ages 13 and over.

cards.title: Leave a name inside Cullen Tower
cards.subtitle: Tower Society rite for graduating seniors
cards.notes: Eligible seniors can follow Tower Society instructions to sign inside Cullen Tower; treat it as a sanctioned ceremony, not an unsupervised climb.
cards.short_summary: Graduating students add their names to a tower whose oldest known signature dates to 1912.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern says seniors have signed Cullen Tower for more than a century and that the Tower Society made the practice an official University tradition.
cards.source_title: A Brief History of the Cullen Building
cards.access_notes: Participation is for graduating seniors through the University’s Tower Society process; do not enter the tower independently.

cards.title: Receive a ring, then ring the bell
cards.subtitle: Alumni ceremony in Lois Perkins Chapel
cards.notes: Students with sufficient credits who order an approved Southwestern ring can confirm ceremony participation and share the occasion with family.
cards.short_summary: A ring presentation ceremony that includes an alumni speaker and the historic bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern calls its Ring Ceremony a special tradition and says it includes ring presentation, family participation, and an opportunity to ring the Rutersville Bell.
cards.access_notes: The cited ceremony required 75 or more credits and an ordered ring; vendor deadlines and event dates vary.

cards.title: Begin as an officially welcomed Pirate
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week induction ceremony
cards.notes: New students can attend the formal Welcome Week ceremony that marks entry into Southwestern’s learning community before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: Southwestern’s annual ceremony formally welcomes and inducts entering students.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern describes Matriculation Convocation as an annual event that begins the academic year and marks students’ official induction into the community.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Welcome Week; the University’s 2026 schedule lists it in Lois Perkins Chapel.

cards.title: Sign the Honor Pledge
cards.subtitle: Academic-integrity practice across designated work
cards.notes: When an instructor designates work for the pledge, write and sign it exactly as required to reaffirm Southwestern’s student-established Honor Code.
cards.short_summary: A more-than-century-old pledge woven into Southwestern’s academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern says students established the Honor Code over a century ago and write and sign the Honor Pledge on examinations, papers, quizzes, and other designated assignments.
cards.access_notes: Use it on professor-designated work; it is an academic-integrity commitment rather than a public event.

cards.title: Take a finals-week karaoke break
cards.subtitle: Breakfast and singing after dark
cards.notes: Watch for finals-week announcements and join the breakfast-and-karaoke gathering for a scheduled break from studying with other students.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding finals-week event built around breakfast, karaoke, and a pause from exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern identifies Late-Night Breakfast as a long-running tradition that gives students a break from finals and includes karaoke.
cards.access_notes: The cited event was scheduled at 10:00 p.m. during finals week; confirm current timing, location, and dining arrangements.

cards.title: Show research at RCWS
cards.subtitle: Annual undergraduate presentation day
cards.notes: Submit or attend presentations, posters, panels, exhibits, and creative work during Southwestern’s all-day undergraduate research showcase.
cards.short_summary: A yearly campus forum where students present scholarly and creative projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern calls the Research and Creative Works Symposium an annual tradition hosted by the Center for Integrative Learning, with posters, oral presentations, exhibits, and panels.
cards.access_notes: Held annually; presentation eligibility, deadlines, and locations are set for each year’s event.

cards.title: Recognize Thicc Man Thursday
cards.subtitle: Pirate offensive-line dinner tradition
cards.notes: This is a football offensive-line tradition: follow the team’s public coverage rather than assuming the gathering is an open student event.
cards.short_summary: Since 2017, Southwestern offensive linemen have gathered on Thursdays during football season to build bonds over dinner.
cards.evidence_claim: Southwestern reports that its offensive linemen have gathered every Thursday evening during football season since 2017 for the tradition called Thicc Man Thursday.
cards.source_title: Southwestern Pirates’ “Thicc Man Thursday” Tradition Builds Camaraderie Among Football Players
cards.access_notes: The reported gathering is for football offensive linemen at an off-campus Whataburger during football season.
